why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief. Builder step 1 gives the cases "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042'; padLeft('42', 5) === '   42'". Verifier Check 1 runs those same two calls and expects "00042" "   42", so the builder gets inputs with expected outputs from the verifier's probe. Builder step 3 repeats '42', 5, '0' -> '00042' as a required test. Builder step 4 also tells the builder to "confirm every name exported from index.js has a `## <name>(` heading in README.md", which is the same check as the verifier's Check 3 probe (each exported name matched against a README heading). Running npm test is allowed, but these repeats hand the builder the checker's own methods.
